name: UI Skills
description: Curated design-engineering skills, Design.md references, playbooks, and an MCP/CLI catalog for agents.
why: The best starting point for UI-focused agents: routing skills, accessibility fixes, motion performance, and design-system extraction.

name: ibelick/ui-skills
description: Source repository for UI Skills: routing, baseline UI, canvas, accessibility, metadata, motion performance, and improve-ui skills.
why: Vendorable, permissively licensed design skills from a well-known design engineer.

name: shadcn/ui
description: Copy-paste React components built on Radix primitives and Tailwind CSS.
why: The default component layer for many production React apps; agents can read the source directly.

name: Radix UI
description: Unstyled, accessible React primitives for dialogs, menus, popovers, tabs, and more.
why: Accessibility and interaction behaviour that agents should reuse instead of rebuilding.

name: Tailwind CSS
description: Utility-first CSS framework with a design-token-friendly configuration.
why: The most common styling layer in agent-generated frontends; its scale and tokens keep output consistent.

name: Motion
description: Production animation library for React and JavaScript, formerly Framer Motion.
why: Springs, gestures, layout transitions, and reduced-motion handling with a stable API.

name: Aceternity UI
description: Copy-paste animated components and landing-page sections for React and Next.js.
why: A large source of polished hero, card, and background patterns; check per-component terms before shipping.

name: Magic UI
description: Open-source animated React components built with Tailwind and Motion.
why: Useful motion-heavy UI blocks without hand-writing every animation.

name: 21st.dev
description: Community registry of React UI components and agent-ready component prompts.
why: Fast way to find a specific component pattern; verify each component's license.

name: Uiverse
description: Community library of CSS and Tailwind UI elements.
why: Good for isolated buttons, loaders, and micro-components; check individual licenses.

name: Lucide
description: Consistent open-source icon set with framework packages.
why: A safe default icon system for agent-generated interfaces.

name: Phosphor Icons
description: Flexible icon family with multiple weights and framework packages.
why: Useful when a design needs weight variation rather than a single stroke style.

name: Heroicons
description: SVG icons from the Tailwind CSS team, in outline, solid, and mini variants.
why: Pairs naturally with Tailwind-based interfaces.

name: Google Fonts
description: Large catalog of open-source typefaces with web embedding.
why: Reliable default for typography when no brand font exists.

name: Fontshare
license: free for personal and commercial use (per font)
description: Curated free typefaces from Indian Type Foundry.
why: A stronger editorial alternative to the most overused Google Fonts.

name: Coolors
description: Palette generator with contrast and export tools.
why: Fast way to explore a palette before encoding semantic tokens.

name: Realtime Colors
description: Preview color palettes and typography on a realistic page layout.
why: Tests a palette in context instead of on a swatch grid.

name: Astryx
description: Meta's open-source, customizable, agent-ready design system with React components, themes, and an Astryx CLI.
why: A production design system that agents can query directly through the astryx command.

name: dqnamo
description: Interaction experiments and component ideas from a London design-engineering studio.
why: High-quality reference for motion, physical UI, and unusual component behaviour.

name: Refactoring UI
description: Design book and resources by Adam Wathan and Steve Schoger for developers.
why: The clearest practical system for hierarchy, spacing, color, and depth. Link only; do not copy.

name: Emil Kowalski skills
description: Animation, motion review, Apple-design, gestures, and UI-library selection skills.
why: Some of the strongest practical motion guidance available as installable skills.

name: Impeccable
description: A flagship design skill for production-grade, anti-generic frontend interfaces.
why: Strong craft constraints and consistency rules for agent-built UI.

name: Taste Skill
description: High-agency UX/UI guidance with layout variance, typography, and GSAP motion constraints.
why: Pushes agents away from templated layouts and toward deliberate visual composition.

name: Vivid Sites
description: Cinematic Three.js and scroll-film website templates with copy-paste prompts.
why: Useful reference for cinematic web direction. Free samples only: /t/prisma, /t/foldworld, /t/blockhaus. Do not copy paid prompts.

name: GetLayers
description: Cinematic AI website template library with prompt-based workflows and an MCP/Figma surface.
why: Reference only. Pricing is paid; no template content is copied into this repository.

name: Inkscape PDF export guide
description: The Inkscape guide explains saving a PDF from an editable SVG and choosing export settings for text and filters.
why: Keep the SVG master, then inspect the exported PDF at its intended size.

name: Figma component naming and organization
description: Figma documents component naming and organization within the Assets panel.
why: Use consistent groups to make components discoverable in a Figma design file.
